raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Fix appended-image prefix-cache misses on Mamba-attention hybrids with APC and Mamba `align`, including producers with a long text tail. Addresses the reproduced case in #43587, not every reported configuration.

## Claims

- Materialize and retain the shared multimodal checkpoint, including the lower checkpoint required by EAGLE/MTP.
- Preserve shared multimodal prefill splits when an image is appended, resolving the observed cached-versus-cold numerical mismatch in the tested configurations.

## Validation

Head `c47defba23`: **530 CPU tests and the real-LLM regression pass**.

| Configuration, 448px | Sequential cached vs cold token IDs / full top-10 logprobs |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5-4B, TP2 default CUDA graphs, 512 tokens | Exact across three multimodal cases and a text control; sibling hits 528 / 2112 / 2112 / 4224 tokens |
| Qwen3.5-4B, TP1 default CUDA graphs, MTP, 512 tokens, long tail | Exact with legacy and lookahead hashes, with nonzero draft acceptance; sibling hits 1632 / 2176 tokens |
| Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 AutoRound, TP1 eager, 512 tokens, long tail | Exact; sibling hit 2352 tokens |
| Qwen3.5-4B, FP8 KV/BF16 SSM, TP1/TP2 default CUDA graphs, 512 tokens | Exact for appended images (2176-token hit at both TP sizes); TP1 vision-enabled text replay also matches exactly, including a 51,826-token prompt with a 51,680-token hit |
| Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 AutoRound, FP8 KV/BF16 SSM, TP1 default CUDA graphs / TP2 eager, 512 tokens | Exact; appended-image hit improves from 0 on base to 2400 tokens on head, with the same head hit at TP2. TP1's 51,864-token text prompt also matches exactly, with a 51,200-token hit |

Unless marked otherwise, GPU checks use FP32 SSM/BF16 KV. Sampling is greedy with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`. Comparisons are sequential within one engine; cold means `skip_reading_prefix_cache=True`, not a fresh process. Strict equality is a fixed-configuration observation, not a general batch-invariance guarantee. The contributed LLM test uses the unchanged upstream `check_logprobs_close`. DCP=2/TP=8 has real CPU Scheduler/cache coverage; the eight-GPU run is deferred because that hardware is unavailable.

<details>
<summary>Concurrency and decode-preemption recovery</summary>

Four-request pressure tests observe overlapping decodes, preemption after output tokens have been produced, and an actual cache hit on the recovered batch's state before isolated references can overwrite it:

| Model / SSM / KV | Output tokens per request | Post-recovery cached tokens | Comparison with isolated cold reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4B / FP32 / BF16 | 512 | 5280 | Upstream closeness passes |
| 27B / BF16 / FP8 | 2048 | 4800 | Upstream closeness passes |
| 27B / FP32 / BF16 | 2048 | 4704 | Upstream closeness passes |

These checks use unchanged upstream `check_logprobs_close` (mutual top-10 membership at the first divergent token), not strict equality. A separate matched base/head batch control also shows strict batch-versus-isolated differences on both commits; they are retained, not counted as exact passes. A 4B FP8/BF16 2048-token workload additionally verifies decode-preemption recovery. Settings match the sequential tests, with four distinct session prefixes and cache-block budgets of 48 (4B FP32), 56 (4B BF16/FP8), or 40 (27B) to force memory pressure.

The 4B FP8/BF16 live-producer check admits the appended-image request after the producer emits 64 of 512 tokens. Decode intervals overlap, the sibling hits 2176 cached tokens, and the upstream comparison passes; strict equality does not.

</details>

<details>
<summary>End-to-end performance, TP1 default CUDA graphs</summary>

Base `317081fb6d` versus head, same RTX A6000; 12 pairs per workload after two excluded warmup rounds. Continuous GPU process monitoring found no foreign processes. Values are median paired elapsed-time ratios (head/base), with bootstrap 95% intervals; smaller is faster. Cache priming and model startup are outside the measurement. Images are synthetic and repeated; cold refers only to APC reads, not forced-cold image encoding.

| Workload | 4B: FP32 SSM/BF16 KV | 27B: BF16 SSM/FP8 KV |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text cold prefill, 1 output token | 0.998 [0.979, 1.026] | 1.007 [1.003, 1.011] |
| Five-image cold prefill, 1 output token | 1.132 [1.117, 1.144] | 1.020 [1.018, 1.025] |
| 32-image cold prefill, 1 output token | 1.230 [1.223, 1.237] | 1.028 [1.024, 1.031] |
| Four-to-five-image cached append, 1 output token | 0.682 [0.680, 0.692] | 0.574 [0.571, 0.576] |
| Four text requests, 128 output tokens each | 1.000 [0.998, 1.003] | 1.0015 [0.9998, 1.0023] |
| Four five-image requests, 128 output tokens each | 1.005 [1.002, 1.010] | 1.0013 [0.9992, 1.0048] |

Each pair resets APC; the cached case primes four images before appending the fifth (base hit 0, head hit 2112/2400 for 4B/27B). Other cases skip prefix-cache reads. Images are 448px; five-image prompts have 5351/5389 tokens and text prompts 4326/4364. Settings: `max_model_len=16384`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=4`, `kv_cache_memory_bytes=2*1024**3`, greedy sampling with `ignore_eos=True`.

4B uses randomized adjacent pairs with persistent engines and warmed MM caches. To fit 27B, paired rounds randomize commit order and use the same shuffled case order; only one engine is awake at a time. Sleep/wakeup and weight transfers are excluded, and clear the processor cache between rounds.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests and reproduction</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_HYBRID_MM_TEST_MODEL="$MODEL4B"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py::test_apc_appended_multimodal_item
```

Before/after evidence:

| Regression selector | Before runtime | Test source | Before result | Fixed result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `incremental_multimodal_sibling` | `317081fb6d` | `be5654d8ef` | 2 failed: `assert 0 == 528` / `assert 0 == 1600` | 2 passed at `be5654d8ef`; 4 cases pass at head |
| `eagle_multimodal_sibling` | `be5654d8ef` | Head | 4 failed / 4 passed controls | 8 passed |
| `dcp_multimodal_sibling` | `5420c48dbf` | Head | 3 failed / 5 passed controls | 8 passed |

To repeat a row, install its before runtime in `OLD_RUNTIME_PYTHON`, export `TEST_SOURCE` for its test checkout and `TEST_FILTER` for its selector, and run outside either checkout:

```bash
env -u PYTHONPATH CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu "$OLD_RUNTIME_PYTHON" - <<'PY'
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import vllm
assert not Path(vllm.__file__).resolve().is_relative_to(Path(os.environ["TEST_SOURCE"]).resolve())
sys.path.insert(0, os.environ["TEST_SOURCE"])
import pytest
raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
    "--import-mode=importlib", "-q",
    os.environ["TEST_SOURCE"] + "/tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py",
    "-k", os.environ["TEST_FILTER"],
]))
PY
```

These before runs intentionally fail. Run the same tests with the installed fixed runtime to verify the passing results. The partition regression also fails upstream with `[[320], [384]]` instead of `[[256, 320], [256, 320]]`; both cache-read settings pass at head.

Reproduce the sequential GPU comparisons with the [archived reproducer](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/vllm/blob/d1e91c0416710fc399296aaf743539ac976bb164/examples/features/automatic_prefix_caching/multimodal_mamba.py) against the installed head. Save it as `multimodal_mamba.py`:

```bash
export VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python multimodal_mamba.py \
  --model "$MODEL4B" --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-tokens 512 --strict
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python multimodal_mamba.py \
  --model "$MODEL27B" --revision 1f05c441c4e64ae0549de44fa9ea5a6d43610314 \
  --enforce-eager --max-tokens 512 --cases long_tail --strict
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python multimodal_mamba.py \
  --model "$MODEL4B" --mtp --max-tokens 512 --legacy-hashes --cases long_tail --strict
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python multimodal_mamba.py \
  --model "$MODEL4B" --mtp --max-tokens 512 --cases long_tail --strict
```

For the FP8 checks, set the reproducer's `LLM` kwargs to `kv_cache_dtype="fp8"`, `mamba_ssm_cache_dtype="bfloat16"` and run the `long_tail` case with 512 output tokens. The long text check sets the `text` case's tail repetition count to 10,000, `max_model_len=65536`, `max_num_batched_tokens=2048`, and 4/8 GiB KV cache for 4B/27B, then runs `--cases text --max-tokens 512 --strict`.

With those FP8 kwargs, reproduce the 27B TP2 eager check with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 .venv/bin/python multimodal_mamba.py --model "$MODEL27B" --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enforce-eager --max-tokens 512 --cases long_tail --strict`.

Hardware/software: RTX A6000 48 GB, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, Transformers 5.17.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1. Set `MODEL4B` to the local ModelScope `Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B` snapshot (weights/config `fcb1a040bb418b0b8add6f6f6c475386abc2cb97`, tokenizer config/chat template `f09dfc75214c5f2f4940ae6a26c126ce93828a9b`); `MODEL27B` to `dbirks/Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-AutoRound` at the revision above. The 27B artifact is not reporter-confirmed original weights.

The independently installed Python-only wheel reuses verified, unchanged native extensions; no fresh native compilation is claimed.

</details>

## Details

Attention hashes can match while no Mamba state remains at the shared image prefix: prefill may skip that boundary, or sparse retention may discard it. The fix makes the final multimodal grid boundary both a prefill stop and a retention point. EAGLE/MTP's fallback is one joint scheduler block lower, keeping generation and retention consistent under DCP's larger attention blocks.

Stopping only at the final image also changes earlier prefill partitions after another image is appended. In the 448px reproducer, identical inputs and weights produce different BF16 gate projections at `M=528` versus `M=2640`; changing only those gates reproduces the GDN difference. All 24 SSM restores are byte-exact. Preserving each multimodal grid boundary resolves this case without changing arithmetic or decode.

Limits: extra prefill stops have measurable cold-prefill cost (13% for five images, 23% for 32 images in the 4B benchmark above), and retained states consume cache capacity. No latency or general batch-invariance guarantee is claimed. The vision-enabled text-only zero-hit report was not reproduced on the tested 4B/27B prompts, including over 51k input tokens. FP8 KV + MTP + FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 fails the sync checker on an unpinned host copy on both base and head; it is not counted as passing. Triton's native-FP8 alternative rejects SM86 hardware. The existing rejection of `align` plus `--disable-chunked-mm-input` is unchanged.

Unlike application-directed checkpoints (#55873/#55875/#55876) or prompt-boundary lifetime protection (#61282), this fix adds automatic multimodal grid checkpoints. Precision defaults, hash format and kernels are unchanged. AI assistance was used.

Upstream [CI admission](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/40817673197/job/123262472138) fails its contributor-label/merge-count gate; downstream code checks are skipped. The [docs-preview check](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35489365/) stopped at the same admission gate, before MkDocs ran.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

 Choose a value that divides the block size of every prefix-cacheable KV cache group, and that is a multiple of the per-state compression ratio for models that use one, such as sparse MLA. vLLM validates both at startup and names the offending sizes in the error. Read the served block size from the startup log. 64 is a reasonable starting point.
 
+### Incremental multimodal requests
+
+With APC enabled, hybrid Mamba models also retain a checkpoint at the final multimodal feature boundary, rounded down to the Mamba block grid. A follow-up request that appends another image can reuse this state even when the producer has a long text tail. No additional checkpoint flag is required. Mamba `align` mode requires multimodal input chunking (the default); combining it with `--disable-chunked-mm-input` is rejected at startup.
+
+Prefill stops at each distinct block-aligned multimodal feature boundary, so appending an item preserves the shared prefix's split points. EAGLE/MTP also materializes a checkpoint one scheduler block lower, to leave room for the draft KV proof or lookahead hash. Under decode context parallelism (DCP), this can span multiple Mamba blocks. Both final-item checkpoints are required retention points, including with the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`; other snapshots follow the configured retention policy. These stops can add prefill work; they do not change decode arithmetic. The shared prefix must contain a cacheable Mamba boundary (and, for EAGLE/MTP, its proof). This does not guarantee batch invariance across different batching or chunk-budget configurations.
+
